title: Billing and Coding: Lumbar Spine MRI
raw_html:
Billing and Coding Article A56542: Lumbar Spine MRI

CPT Coding Guidance

This billing and coding article accompanies LCD L33822 and defines payable CPT codes, professional/technical component modifiers, and covered ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for lumbar spine MRI claims.

CPT CodeDescriptionAllowed Modifiers
72148MRI lumbar spine without contrast material26 (Professional), TC (Technical)
72149MRI lumbar spine with contrast material26 (Professional), TC (Technical)
72158MRI lumbar spine without contrast followed by with contrast26 (Professional), TC (Technical)

ICD-10-CM Coding Notes

Claims billed without a qualifying diagnosis such as low back pain (M54.50), lumbar intervertebral disc disorder with radiculopathy (M51.16), or cauda equina syndrome (G83.4) will deny as not medically necessary.

title: Policy Article: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices - Documentation and Modifier KX
raw_html:
Policy Article A52467: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices Documentation

Modifier KX Requirements

Suppliers must append modifier KX to HCPCS codes E0601, E0470, and mask interface supplies (A7030) only when all coverage criteria in LCD L33718—including qualifying sleep study and 90-day adherence compliance—are documented on file.

HCPCS CodeItem DescriptionModifier Rule
E0601Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) deviceAppend KX when coverage criteria met
E0470Respiratory assist device, bi-level without backup rateRequires documented CPAP intolerance plus KX
A7030Full face mask used with PAP deviceEligible for replacement every 3 months with KX

Face-to-Face Re-Evaluation Timing

If the 31-to-91-day adherence evaluation occurs late, coverage resumes prospectively only after the re-evaluation is completed and compliance is verified.

title: Billing and Coding: Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGM)
raw_html:
Billing and Coding Article A57690: Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGM)

Coverage and Billing Criteria

Medicare covers adjunctive and non-adjunctive continuous glucose monitors (E2102, E2103) and monthly supply allowances (A4239) for beneficiaries with diabetes mellitus who are treated with insulin or have a history of problematic level 2 or level 3 hypoglycemia.

HCPCS CodeDescriptionBilling Frequency
E2102Adjunctive continuous glucose monitor receiverOne receiver per 5-year reasonable useful lifetime
E2103Non-adjunctive, non-implanted CGM receiverOne receiver per 5-year reasonable useful lifetime
A4239Supply allowance for non-adjunctive CGM sensors/transmitters1 unit per month

Beneficiary Follow-Up

Treating practitioners must conduct an in-person or Medicare-approved telehealth visit within 6 months prior to ordering CGM and every 6 months thereafter to assess glycemic adherence.

title: Billing and Coding: Mohs Micrographic Surgery
raw_html:
Billing and Coding Article A56632: Mohs Micrographic Surgery

Covered Anatomic Sites and Coding

Mohs micrographic surgery is covered for basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma on high-risk anatomic areas including the face, nose, eyelids, ears, lips, hands, feet, and genitalia, or for recurrent and aggressive histologic subtypes.

CPT CodeAnatomic Region and StageBilling Rule
17311Head, neck, hands, feet, genitalia; first stage, up to 5 tissue blocksRequires surgeon to act as both surgeon and pathologist
17312Each additional stage after first stage (head/neck/hands/feet/genitalia)Add-on code billed with 17311
17313Trunk, arms, or legs; first stage, up to 5 tissue blocksCovered for high-risk or recurrent lesions

Pathology Bundling

Separate surgical pathology codes (88305) are not separately payable on the same lesion treated with Mohs surgery because frozen-section margin mapping is bundled into 17311-17315.
